summary: The polity led by the first four caliphs after Muhammad’s death expanded from Arabia into Byzantine and Sasanian territories.
rulers: Selected rulers: Umar ibn al-Khattab, 634–644; Ali ibn Abi Talib, 656–661.
military: Arab armies conquered territories including Egypt, Syria and Iraq, taking advantage of weakened Byzantine and Sasanian power.
contributions: Established the first caliphal governments outside Arabia and founded Fustat as an administrative center in Egypt.
origin: Leadership of the Muslim community passed to caliphs following Muhammad’s death in 632.
decline: Civil conflict and Ali’s assassination preceded Muawiya’s establishment of Umayyad dynastic rule in 661.
periodNote: The conventional period ends in 661; succession and legitimacy were contested, and “Rightly Guided” is a traditional designation.
